ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, general partners, limited partners, directors and authorized signatories against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the Canadian Global Affairs Canada Consolidated Sanctions List, and lists maintained under the Special Economic Measures Act. Prudent market practice also requires screening against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List. Foreign and domestic politically exposed persons as defined in SOR/2018-32 must receive enhanced due diligence including source of wealth, source of funds, business rationale and senior management approval. Terrorist financing indicators under Criminal Code section 83.01 and the United Nations Act must be reviewed before any transfer of funds.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ontario Business Registry (OnBiz), operated by the Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery / Companies and Personal Property Security Branch
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Ontario accepts English and French names. Names in other scripts must be transliterated into the Roman alphabet and must be capable of being represented in the Ontario Business Registry. The name may not be obscene, scandalous, misleading or contrary to public interest. An Ontario limited partnership must use its registered name in Ontario and must not carry on business under a name that is confusing with a pre-existing registered business name or trade-mark.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejection must be evidenced by a written refusal notice identifying the statutory or naming grounds. The applicant may file a formal reconsideration request with the Registrar, Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, within 30 days of refusal, attaching a fresh NUANS or Ontario Business Registry name search report, the grounds of rebuttal, and any consent letters from professional regulators if the name contains a sensitive token. If the Registrar declines to reverse the rejection, the aggrieved applicant may apply for judicial review to the Ontario Divisional Court under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. J.1, within 90 days of the final refusal. A new name search is mandatory if the original report exceeds the validity window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A licensed commercial virtual office is acceptable for registry and service-of-process address purposes only. For an immigration and international student placement advisory business, a standalone virtual mailbox is not recommended and is unlikely to satisfy the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC) professional standards. The licensee should maintain a physical Canadian place of business with client files, a responsible professional physically available, and audit-ready records. Virtual offices are permissible only as supplementary correspondence addresses for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate quantified risk: approximately 25-35% probability of an unannounced on-site compliance inspection within the first 12 months of licensing. The probability rises to 45-55% if the sole declared address is a virtual office or private residential suite.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ontario Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. L.8, as amended (particularly ss. 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 and 9); Business Names Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. B.11; Limited Partnerships Regulation (Ontario Reg. 358/90); Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, s. 91 (immigration consultant licensing context); College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants Act, S.C. 2019, c. 29, s. 293.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, Companies and Personal Property Security Branch; filings are submitted through ServiceOntario, Central Production and Verification Services.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration under Section 3 of the Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. L.8, in the form approved by the Minister; related business name registration is incorporated in the Ontario business registry record.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to Ontario limited partnerships. For this regulated advisory business, however, agreed limited partner capital contributions must be actually advanced and held in escrow in Ontario before client immigration funds are accepted, and the general partner must maintain an Ontario-registered office and, if a non-resident, appoint an Ontario-resident attorney for service.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscription offered to Limited Partners upon the terms set in the Confidential Offering Memorandum is approved, and the General Partner is authorized to admit each subscriber who executes the Partnership Agreement and delivers the agreed capital contribution to the escrow account. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Limited Partnership is established at the Ontario street address identified in the Declaration, and the General Partner may change such address in accordance with the Limited Partnerships Act. RESOLVED, that the named individuals are appointed as officers and managing agents; the Compliance Officer is authorized to hold the immigration consultant licence; and each officer may open bank accounts and execute statutory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Name Search and Preliminary Name Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ServiceOntario Central Names and Business Information Registry; concurrent NUANS search through approved service providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a Canadian automated NUANS name search to identify conflicting corporate, partnership, and trademark names. Propose a name that must end with 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.' and is distinguishable from existing records. If immediate filing is not possible, file a 90-day name reservation through ServiceOntario. Retain the NUANS search report as part of the eventual declaration filing.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report
Proposed registered LP name, with acceptable alternatives
Consent letter of any living individual or entity whose name appears in the proposed name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or flagged as confusing, submit a written distinguishability argument or obtain a written consent from the prior owner; alternatively withdraw the name and refile with a substantially different name, avoiding an additional filing penalty where the initial declaration has not yet been accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Declaration and Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, Companies and Personal Property Security Branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Declaration under section 3 of the Limited Partnerships Act, stating the LP name, Ontario registered office address, full names and addresses of all general partners, their status as resident or non-resident, and the agreed contribution or obligation to contribute. Draft and execute a limited partnership agreement addressing capital accounts, profit sharing, withdrawals, admission of limited partners, tax pass-through elections, and the authority of the general partner and officers.
required_dossiers: Completed Declaration under the Limited Partnerships Act
Executed Limited Partnership Agreement
Consent of the registered office provider and Ontario agent for service
Certified identification documents of each general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the branch queries a declaration item, amend the form with a covering explanation and re-file; foreign executions must be notarized or apostilled as required, and any discrepancy in the registered office address must be corrected before acceptance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: E-Filing of the Declaration with ServiceOntario
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ServiceOntario, Central Production and Verification Services; Ontario Companies and Personal Property Security Branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Declaration online through the ServiceOntario business e-filing channel or by counter filing at the Ontario Business Office. Pay the prescribed filing fee, receive the ServiceOntario transaction number, and preserve the electronic acknowledgement as proof of recor d. Verify that all general partner names and the Ontario registered office are entered exactly as executed in the final document.
required_dossiers: Signed and completed Declaration
NUANS report and name reservation acknowledgement
Filing fee payment receipt
Authorization letter from the general partner to the filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query or correction notice, submit the corrected Declaration under the correction process or file an amended declaration, paying only the incremental fee where the original record is amended before extraction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Registry Record and LP Information Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Companies and Personal Property Security Branch / ServiceOntario Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After acceptance, obtain the endorsed registry record and request an Ontario business information extract evidencing the legal existence, registered office, and general partner details of the limited partnership. Distribute the extract to the bank, tax advisor, and immigration regulator as proof of formation.
required_dossiers: ServiceOntario filing receipt and transaction number
Registry extract request authorization
Identification of the requesting authorized officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry extract contains a transcribed error, file a statement of change under section 7 of the Limited Partnerships Act with supporting evidence and pay the administrative correction fee; if the extract is delayed, escalate through the ServiceOntario registry support line with the transaction number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Ontario Business Registration and Tax Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ServiceOntario; Canada Revenue Agency; Ontario Ministry of Finance; Workplace Safety and Insurance Board
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the limited partnership for a federal business number and applicable accounts (GST/HST, payroll, corporate income tax where required). Confirm the Ontario business registry shows the LP name and address, and obtain a WSIB clearance letter where the partnership will have employees. Where applicable, register for Ontario employer health tax and provincial tax accounts.
required_dossiers: Ontario registry endorsement or business information extract
General partner identification and business number application
Proof of Ontario registered office address
Payroll and employment information, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or Ontario accounts are not activated within the expected timeline, follow up through My Business Account or the Ontario Tax Service Line; if late filings occur, apply for taxpayer relief explaining the delay and submit supporting evidence for waiver of penalties and interest.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Banking, Escrow and Immigration Regulatory Readiness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Schedule-regulated Canadian financial institution; College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC); Ontario Private Career Colleges supervisory unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the partnership operating bank account and segregated client escrow account, complete enhanced due diligence and know-your-client forms, and execute the escrow agreement for client funds related to study abroad and immigration visa services. Appoint or engage a Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant, approve the AML/ATF compliance program and partnership register, and register the business as an international student placement agent where Ontario private career college enrollment services are provided.
required_dossiers: Ontario registry extract confirming legal existence
Executed partnership agreement and officer resolutions
AML/ATF policy, risk assessment, and client identification protocols
RCIC licence or sponsorship/engagement agreement with licensed consultant
Bank and escrow mandate documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional KYC information, provide source-of-funds declarations, partnership org charts, and updated utility bills; if the CICC registration is refused, submit a written reconsideration within 30 days and, until resolved, ensure a licensed RCIC is engaged under the authorized CICC regulatory framework.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC); Ontario Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development; Ontario Ministry of Colleges and Universities (Private Career Colleges Act, 2005)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) licence; Ontario international student placement agent registration; Master Business Licence for the limited partnership

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks (MECP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Office and Advisory Use Only; no full Environmental Impact Assessment report required because the partnership performs no manufacturing, industrial processing, or discharge of effluent from the business premises
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, stormwater discharge, or industrial VOC emissions are generated. Tenant fit-out, if any, must comply with Ontario Regulation 419/05 air pollution limits and the hosting municipality's sewer by-law (generally pH 6.0-9.5, BOD less than 50 mg/L, TSS less than 50 mg/L); HVAC refrigerants must be handled under O. Reg 270/16; all non-hazardous office waste must be removed by a licensed waste carrier under the Ontario EPA and municipal waste management bylaws.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Approved fire safety plan and fire extinguisher inspection under the Ontario Fire Code; confirmation that the leased premises' structural load ratings accommodate office occupancy; workplace hazard assessment and first-aid readiness under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. O.1; WSIB clearance letter confirming workplace insurance coverage; and, where opened to clients, public access and emergency evacuation signage approved by the provincial fire marshal.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada - national tax authority for federal income tax and GST/HST. Portal: CRA My Business Account (MyBA), accessible via Business Registration Online (BRO). Ontario provincial counterpart: Ontario Ministry of Finance, responsible only for Employer Health Tax and land transfer tax; all income tax and HST are administered federally through the CRA under the Tax Collection Agreement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the Limited Partnership under the Ontario Limited Partnerships Act (R.S.O. 1990, c. L.2) through the Ontario Business Registry; a foreign extra-provincial LP must complete equivalent extra-provincial registration. Step 2: Obtain a CRA Business Number (BN) for the LP using Business Registration Online or paper Form RC1; the LP must create an RT program account for GST/HST, an RP account for employer payroll remittances, and an RM account for import/export transactions where applicable. Step 3: Register voluntarily for GST/HST under the Excise Tax Act if input tax credits are desired prior to exceeding the small supplier threshold. Step 4: Open the CRA MyBA account, link the BN, and authorize a representative via the Represent a Client service. Step 5: File the annual partnership information return (T5013) and, for every non-resident partner, T5013F and T5013-SUM; remit any applicable Part XIII withholding on distributions to non-resident partners. Step 6: For regulated immigration-visa advisory activity, the LP must ensure its advisers are licensed by the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC); CICC licence is a regulatory prerequisite and must be referenced in the CRA record of business.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box election; an Ontario-registered Limited Partnership is mandatorily fiscally transparent under ITA s. 96. Available elections: (1) joint election under ITA s. 97(2) to transfer eligible capital property into the LP on a tax-deferred basis; (2) elections under ITA s. 98(3)/(4) to defer tax on distributions on partnership dissolution; (3) voluntary GST/HST registration election under ETA s. 240(1) for a small supplier; (4) GST Quick Method election under ETA s. 225.1 for businesses with annual worldwide GST-included taxable supplies of C$400,000 or less; (5) annual GST/HST filing election under ETA s. 238(1) instead of quarterly filing; (6) partnership agreement allocation of profits and losses, provided the split is commercially reasonable and not arbitrary.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax); Ontario HST comprises the federal 5% GST component plus the 8% Ontario provincial component, administered jointly by the CRA on taxable supplies made in Ontario.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 - the small supplier threshold is measured on worldwide gross revenues from taxable supplies (excluding exempt supplies and financial services) in a single calendar quarter or over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; voluntary registration is available below the threshold to claim input tax credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, QR digital stamping, or government e-invoice authorisation regime exists in Canada as of the 2025 tax year. The CRA accepts paper, PDF, and E-invoice records and requires GST/HST returns to be transmitted via NETFILE, EFILE, or the CRA My Business Account API. Every invoice must satisfy ETA s. 223 by stating the supplier name, the Business Number (RT account), the invoice date, the 13% Ontario HST rate where the supply is taxable, the amount of tax, and, for exports, a clear zero-rated indicator. A voluntary Pan-Canadian B2B e-invoicing framework based on Peppol PINT is available but not yet legally obligatory. For exported goods, the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) requires an electronic export declaration through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CADERS); pure service exports require no customs clearance filing.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For services: Schedule VI, Part V, s. 9 ETA zero-rates a supply of a service made to a non-resident person where the service is not performed while the individual is physically present in Canada and the service is not in respect of real property situated in Canada or tangible personal property situated in Canada. Study-abroad placement, Golden Visa advisory, and immigration-visa consultancy delivered to a non-resident student or client located outside Canada qualify as zero-rated offshore services. If the identical service is rendered to a person while physically present in Canada or is intended to benefit a Canadian resident, it is taxable at 13% HST. For goods: tangible personal property exported as part of the service package (for example, study materials or information kits) may be zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V, s. 7 if the goods are exported within 60 days of the supply and the exemption documentation is retained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Electronic Export Declaration (EED/B13A) - mandatory for exported goods only, not required for a pure service export
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill (for goods) or a signed International Service Agreement / detailed engagement letter (for services)
Inward remittance certificate / bank MT103 SWIFT credit advice evidencing FX receipt from the non-resident client within the 180-day repatriation window
Copy of the foreign client's passport or non-resident certificate evidencing status
Detailed service delivery log documenting that the advisory work was performed outside Canada and for the exclusive benefit of the non-resident recipient
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audit practice tests export zero-rating against the ETA s. 223 record-keeping standard; missing documentation or a failed place-of-supply analysis will cause the supply to be reassessed as taxable at 13% HST, with arrears interest charged on the unremitted amount. A false or careless export claim triggers the ETA s. 285(2) civil penalty of 35% of the amount by which the claimed refund or rebate exceeded the true entitlement; a second or continued misstatement attracts a penalty of 50%. Willful evasion is subject to criminal prosecution under ETA s. 327(1), with fines of up to C$500,000 and imprisonment for up to 12 months. The CRA may further disallow input tax credits, apply the ITA s. 162(7) penalty for late or incomplete T5013 partnership returns, and reopen the export transactions within the six-year ordinary reassessment window for negligence.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (central bank); foreign exchange administration and compliance oversight shared with the Department of Finance Canada, FINTRAC, and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI). Canada does not operate a separate exchange-control authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full convertibility on both current and capital account items. Profit remittance by an Ontario limited partnership is unrestricted, but distributions to non-resident partners are subject to Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act, subject to treaty relief. Cross-border transfers of CAD 10,000 or more must be reported to FINTRAC. Capital account flows, including equity injections and repatriation, are free from administrative approval; however, banks must screen transactions against Canadian sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act, the United Nations Act, and the Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act. CRS/AEoI and FATCA classification obligations also apply to all financial accounts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory surrender or mandatory conversion requirements on export proceeds or service receipts. Exporters and service providers may retain foreign currency freely in Canadian or foreign bank accounts. The only relevant obligations are statistical reporting under the Statistics Act for cross-border transactions above prescribed thresholds (typically CAD 200,000 quarterly) and accurate computation of foreign exchange gains/losses under the Income Tax Act.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low as a statutory escrow provider because capital escrow for immigration and international student services requires a regulated Canadian financial institution or trust company. Medium for non-escrow operational collection and payment flows through registered Money Service Businesses (MSBs). Ontario does not license standalone electronic money institutions; a fintech cross-border payment provider must be registered with FINTRAC and operate settlement accounts through a Schedule I Canadian bank. Offshore digital bank accounts may receive and disburse non-client operational funds but cannot act as trust/escrow accounts under Canadian regulatory practice without express financial institution licensing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canada has no universal statutory mandate requiring directors or general partners to appear physically at a branch. FINTRAC-compliant remote identity verification may be acceptable. However, for a Medium-Risk Enhanced immigration/visa business, most major banks require a video interview or branch visit by the general partner or a senior signing officer. A corporate general partner holding central management and control may need a notarized resolution and certified corporate registry extracts. Remote account opening with EDD is practicable for banks with mature digital onboarding, but transaction closure typically demands in-person confirmation for escrow accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partners or beneficial owners in countries identified as high-risk by FATF or enhanced sanctions lists
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Limited partnership declaration and Certificate of Limited Partnership from the Ontario register; apostilled/notarized corporate extracts for each corporate partner; source-of-wealth letters for all individuals owning 25% or more; professional reference letters from legal or financial advisers in regulated jurisdictions; bank statements or sale-of-asset evidence supporting capital injection provenance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Immigration/visa consulting scope exposing the account to third-party prepayments, refunds, or client funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid license from the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC) or evidence of authorised legal practice exemption; client retainer and service agreements; detailed operating procedures for separate client trust accounting where applicable; escrow agreement with the bank; declaration of compliance with the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and Ontario consumer protection statutes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aggregated large value inbound wire transfers from multiple overseas individuals inconsistent with typical consulting fees
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Invoice register listing each student or visa applicant, unique invoice number, and amount; authenticated admission offer letters from educational institutions or approved immigration approvals; proof of government visa application filings; bank rationale memorandum explaining transaction flows; source-of-funds declarations for each initiating remitter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential sanctions/PEP exposure associated with 'golden visa' countries or politically exposed persons
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions and PEP screening results with clear timestamps; signed declarations from each partner on connection to sanctioned individuals/entities; legal opinion from Canadian counsel on compliance with the Special Economic Measures Act, the United Nations Act, and the Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; updated beneficial ownership register with materiality thresholds; ongoing transaction monitoring policy.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound equity injection must use SWIFT MT103 with the beneficiary account name matching the Ontario limited partnership registration. The purpose field should state 'capital contribution to limited partnership' and include the LP registration number and capital call notice reference. The remitting partner must send from its own bank account; third-party wires are not permitted for equity injection without a formal assignment and certified KYC. Canadian banks must report all international electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more to FINTRAC. The recipient LP must provide a copy of the partnership agreement, a capital call schedule, and FATCA/CRS classification for each partner. Intermediary settlement can be accomplished via SWIFT MT202 COV for cover payments between correspondent banks.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade and service settlements are executed primarily through SWIFT MT103 for direct cross-border payments, including tuition fees to foreign educational institutions and commissioned disbursements to sub-agents. For high-value or secure settlements, a commercial letter of credit (documentary credit) may be issued against invoices or admission documents. Interbank settlement between Canadian and overseas correspondent banks uses SWIFT MT202 COV or local clearing systems such as CHIPS/Fedwire for US dollar legs and Lynx for Canadian dollar legs. Each MT103 must include ISO 20022 purpose codes appropriate to the underlying transaction, for example 'EDUC' for education services or 'CONS' for consulting services, with full remitter/beneficiary legal names and addresses.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or offshore currencies (e.g. offshore RMB, INR, KRW)
Currency futures listed on regulated Canadian or foreign exchanges (e.g. Montreal Exchange)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ontario Limited Partnership Annual Declaration under section 13 of the Limited Partnership Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. L.16
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Director, Companies and Personal Property Security Branch, ServiceOntario, Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, Government of Ontario
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 60 days after each anniversary of the date of registration of the limited partnership; no extension is available in the statute.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts an administrative late-filing charge; continuing default permits the Director to strike the limited partnership from the register. After strike-off the partnership cannot lawfully carry on business in Ontario and general partners may remain personally liable for obligations incurred during or after the default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Partnership Information Return and T5013 Supplementary Income Slips
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually; the T5013 return is due by the earlier of March 31 following the calendar year in which the partnership's fiscal period ends and five months after the fiscal period end; partner information slips must be provided by March 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger penalties under subsection 162(7) of the Income Tax Act, currently C$50 per day up to C$2,500, with additional penalties for repeated default or knowingly false statements; partner filings may be assessed without a complete return.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Immigration Consultant Licence Renewal and Continuing Professional Development Compliance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC), delegated regulator under the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants Act, 2021
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in accordance with the CICC renewal cycle, normally by March 31 each year as published in the current renewal notice; no statutory grace period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-renewal causes automatic lapse of the immigration consultant licence; continued regulated activity is unauthorized practice, subject to CICC discipline, administrative monetary penalties, and prohibition orders under the applicable Ontario legislation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory independent audit applies to a private Ontario limited partnership under the Limited Partnership Act, but an audit becomes compulsory when: (i) a regulated immigration consultant holds client funds and CICC requires an independent trust account examination; (ii) a court orders an accounting or audit in a partner dispute; (iii) the partnership agreement, lender, or investor covenant requires audited annual financial statements; or (iv) the partnership is engaged in a prescribed financial-sector activity under federal or provincial regulations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP under CPA Canada Handbook: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; ASPE for private partnerships and LPs; CRA GIFI schedules must be reconciled to the applicable GAAP-basis financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Ontario does not require a separate annual UBO filing for limited partnerships. The Limited Partnership Act requires an annual declaration identifying current general partners; limited partner transfers are not publicly filed. Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, the immigration visa consultancy must obtain, verify, and periodically rescreen beneficial ownership information for medium-risk clients, and confirm such beneficial ownership on any transfer of a partnership interest and at least at annual rescreening intervals.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200–600 per year for a standard Ontario limited partnership registered office and service agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500–8,500 per engagement for a typical small-entity partnership trust account audit or court-ordered audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined federal and Ontario general corporate rate (15% federal Part I + 11.5% Ontario corporate income tax). An Ontario Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent and is not a taxpayer; corporate general and limited partners are taxable on allocated partnership income at this composite headline rate.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Nil for the Limited Partnership as a separate taxpayer. Eligible Canadian-controlled private corporate partners may claim the federal small business deduction (effective federal rate 9% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income) and Ontario small business deduction (effective Ontario rate 3.2% on the first CAD 500,000), yielding a combined effective rate of approximately 12.2% on qualifying active business income. Service income from study-abroad and immigration advisory activities generally qualifies as active business income for CCPCs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 – Partnership Information Return; filed through CRA-approved electronic software or via a CRA Business Account XML upload using the File Transfer Service (FTS).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than the earliest filing-due date of any partner's return that includes the partnership allocation. For an Ontario LP with a December 31 fiscal year-end and a corporate general partner, the T5013 must be filed by June 30 of the following calendar year (six months after the LP's fiscal year-end).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the Ontario limited partnership, CRA Business Number (BN), Ontario registration number, registered address, and fiscal period start/end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the LP's Canadian BN and ensure the partnership has obtained a CRA account. Non-resident partners must be identified in Schedule 1 with country of residence and applicable treaty-protection indicator.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue, expenses, net income or loss of the partnership classified under GIFI (General Index of Financial Information) codes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Canadian-source revenue attributable to advisory and placement services separately; expenses must be allocated on a reasonable basis. Non-resident partners should not include foreign-source income in this schedule unless directly allocable to their Canadian LP interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Each partner's class (G = General, SL = Specified Limited, L = Limited), ownership percentage, allocation of income/loss, and transfer of tax credits and tax attributes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each non-resident partner, provide full foreign name, residence address, country of tax residence, and the partner's tax identification number or Canadian BN/SIN where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 40 / Schedule 52 – Current-year income and tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of taxable income, non-capital losses, and available investment tax credits among partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners should be assigned only the Canadian-source portion of income or loss. If a non-resident partner claims treaty protection for business profits attributable to no Canadian permanent establishment, the LP must still report the allocation and the partner must file a nil T1/T2 return to assert the treaty position.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Consolidated summary of all partners, their SIN/BN, country of residence, and aggregate allocation amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the non-resident partners' foreign tax reference numbers and confirm whether any Part XIII withholding has been applied to payments from the partnership. For pure business profits, Part XIII withholding is not applicable; the non-resident partner is instead taxed under Part I on the allocated Canadian-source income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted T5013 filing triggers a CRA penalty under ITA s.162(7): CAD 25 per day, up to a maximum of CAD 2,500. Knowingly or negligently making a false statement in the T5013 or a partner's return may trigger a gross-negligence penalty of 50% of the tax payable by any partner that is understated. CRA may also impose interest on any unpaid partner-level tax attributable to the late information return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 – Corporation Income Tax Return; required for any corporate general partner or corporate limited partner subject to Canadian Part I tax on allocated LP income; filed via CRA's Internet File Transfer using approved e-file software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the corporation's taxation year-end. For a corporate partner with a December 31 year-end, the T2 is due by June 30 of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of the partner's share of T5013 income or loss and inclusion in the corporation's taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporate partner carrying on business in Canada through the LP must file Schedule 26 and the T2 return to report Canadian-source business income attributable to the LP. If the non-resident corporate partner is treaty-protected because the LP does not constitute a permanent establishment, it still must file a nil T2 to preserve treaty-relief claims.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 1 – Balance sheet and tax reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial position of the corporation and adjustments between accounting income and taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only assets and liabilities reasonably related to Canadian activities. Non-resident corporations should attach a CRA Schedule 91 for branch accounts where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate of all income, including partnership allocations, less losses, deductions, and exemptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations must apply the limited Canadian-source income rules under ITA s.115, using only amounts traceable to the LP and to services performed in Canada.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal corporate tax computed at 15% of taxable income, before credits, plus any Ontario corporate tax allocation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partners may be subject to Part I tax and, further, Part XIV branch tax on their net Canadian unremitted profits. Treaty relief may be claimed by attaching the foreign certificate of residence and a letter of treaty claim.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of a T2 incurs a 5% penalty on the balance owing plus 1% for each full month, up to 12 months (maximum 17%), and an additional 10% penalty for a second or subsequent failure within three years. Gross negligence or false statements expose the partner to a 50% penalty of the understated tax. Interest at prescribed rates is compounded daily from the original filing deadline.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Ontario Limited Partnership Annual Return (Ontario Ministry of Government and Consumer Services / ServiceOntario online registry portal); not a tax return but mandatory for maintaining the Ontario LP registration.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 60 days after the anniversary of the limited partnership's registration date under the Ontario Limited Partnerships Act (R.S.O. 1990, c. L.16).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Registered name and Ontario LP number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The exact legal name of the limited partnership and its registration number issued by the Ontario Gazette or ServiceOntario.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate the registered office address in Ontario. A non-resident general partner must provide its jurisdiction of residence and an Ontario address for service.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names, addresses, and capacities of all current general partners, and confirmation that no general partner has changed during the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a general partner is non-resident, an Ontario resident representative must be named for service of legal process.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certification that the LP continues to carry on business or intends to recommence business, and that the information is accurate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident general partner's authorized signatory must execute the declaration; if no activity, the LP should complete the declaration accurately or apply for voluntary dissolution to avoid administrative cancellation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the Ontario annual return may result in administrative dissolution or revocation of the LP's registration. Under Ontario's Business Information Act and Corporations Information Act, corporate general partners may face fines up to CAD 2,000 for each failure to update registry information, and the Registrar may refuse to issue a certificate of status.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII on dividends paid by a Canadian resident corporation to a non-resident shareholder. This dividend withholding rate does not apply to distributions from an Ontario Limited Partnership because an LP is fiscally transparent: distributions to partners are a return of capital, loan repayment, or income allocation, not a dividend. Non-resident limited partners are instead taxed under Part I on their allocated share of Canadian-source partnership business income; if the non-resident partner is a corporation and realizes unremitted net Canadian business profits through the LP, a 25% Part XIV branch tax may apply, subject to treaty reduction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty benefits on any Canadian withholding taxes, the non-resident beneficial owner must be resident in a treaty country and must file a Canadian CRA Form NR301 (for individuals) or NR302 (for corporations) with the Canadian payor before the relevant payment is made, together with a Certificate of Residency (TRC) issued by the competent authority of the residence-country tax administration. For business profits allocated by an Ontario LP to a non-resident partner, treaty relief is claimed by filing a Canadian T1/T2 return and attaching the TRC plus a written treaty position. A TRC must be kept contemporaneously and is generally valid only for the calendar year specified.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rates: 25% on interest paid to non-residents, and 25% on royalties for use of intellectual property or know-how. Certain non-arm's-length interest paid by a Canadian payer to a related non-resident may also be denied deductibility if the recipient is not subject to tax (s.18(3.1)). Treaty rates typically reduce arm's-length interest to 0% (Canada-USA) or 10% under some treaties; royalty withholding is commonly reduced to 0%–10% depending on the treaty partner and the class of IP (copyright, industrial process, patents). Study-abroad franchise or branding fees paid by the Ontario LP to a foreign affiliate must be benchmarked at arm's-length and may be subject to treaty-reduced withholding only if the foreign recipient is the real beneficial owner.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 for related-party transactions triggering T106 (Related Party Transactions) reporting and contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation. Multinational enterprise groups with consolidated revenue of at least CAD 750,000,000 are subject to Country-by-Country (CbC) reporting, and Canadian entities in such groups must maintain a Master File and Local File. Under ITA s.247, all cross-border non-arm's-length transactions, irrespective of amount, must be priced on an arm's-length basis.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime akin to certain offshore centres. Instead, the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR), section 247 transfer pricing rules, and treaty 'beneficial ownership' / principal purpose tests impose a substantive economic-meaning requirement. An Ontario LP must have actual commercial purpose, employees, premises, bank accounts, and decision-making in Canada. A passive limited partner with no real investment risk or control may be recharacterized as a financing arrangement or sham; likewise, a non-resident corporate partner claiming treaty benefits must demonstrate residence-based substance and that its Canadian LP profits are not artificially routed. CRA will disregard transactions lacking economic substance and may apply GAAR plus the 25% GAAR penalty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting cash fees from study-abroad placement, immigration, or golden-visa advisory services; inflating management or consultancy fees payable to a related offshore entity; claiming personal expenses as partnership deductions; or misallocating income to a non-resident partner in a zero-rate jurisdiction without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under ITA s.239: fine of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years. CRA civil gross-negligence penalty of 50% of the understated tax under s.163(2), plus daily compound interest on unpaid amounts from the original deadline.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners and directors of the corporate general partner are jointly and severally liable under ITA s.227.1 for unpaid taxes that the partnership failed to remit, and under s.160 for any non-arm's-length transfer of assets to avoid payment. Ontario courts may grant travel bans, asset seizure, equitable tracing, and fraud injunctions against directors and partners.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File Information Returns / T5013 Omission
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the T5013 Partnership Information Return for an Ontario LP with corporate or non-resident partners; omitting a partner's share of income or losses; failing to provide Schedule 50 GIFI or Schedule 1 allocation data.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA penalty under ITA s.162(7): CAD 25 per day, maximum CAD 2,500, for late or omitted information returns. A false statement in the T5013 may lead to a summary conviction offence, a fine of up to CAD 25,000, and a 50% gross-negligence penalty on any partner-level tax payable. Ontario may also administratively cancel the LP registration for non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner, and any limited partner who participates in management or control, becomes personally liable for the partnership's penalty and tax obligations. Directors of a corporate general partner who knowingly fail to cause the partnership to comply can be assessed under s.227.1 and may be prohibited from serving as directors under Ontario corporate law.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Incorrupting an Ontario LP with a single-purpose corporate general partner resident in a no-tax jurisdiction, without staff, premises, books, or performance of actual study-abroad/immigration services, for the principal purpose of diverting fees from Canadian service recipients to a non-resident entity and avoiding Part I tax and Part XIII withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may disregard the limited partnership as a sham or apply GAAR to recharacterize the arrangement; tax benefit is denied, GAAR penalty is 25% of the tax benefit, and transfer-pricing adjustments under s.247(3) attract a 10% penalty (minimum CAD 5,000). The Ontario Registrar may strike the LP from the registry for cessation of business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Limited partners who are involved in the control or management of the LP lose limited liability and become jointly and severally liable for all LP debts. Directors of the corporate general partner owe fiduciary duties and may be personally liable under s.160 and s.227.1 for taxes and penalties, and can be barred from managing another Ontario entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an international-student placement or immigration advisory service while accepting escrow or wire-transfer client funds without registering with FINTRAC as a Money Services Business (MSB) or Foreign Money Services Business (FMSB), failing to report suspicious transactions, failing to implement a risk-based compliance regime, or processing funds known to be derived from fraudulent immigration schemes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, administrative monetary penalties can be up to CAD 100,000 for an individual and CAD 500,000 for a corporation per violation; criminal prosecution for laundering proceeds of crime carries a maximum term of up to 10 years imprisonment and unlimited fines. FINTRAC may publish non-compliance notices and the Federal Court may issue compliance orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers, directors, and general partners who authorize, permit, or acquiesce in a contravention are individually guilty of the offence. They may be subject to criminal prosecution, director disqualification, civil asset forfeiture, and travel restrictions; the corporate veil is penetrated for AML offences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Providing paid immigration advice, visa application assistance, study-permit or golden-visa residence strategies, or immigration-representation services in Canada without the person being a member in good standing of the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (RCIC/ICCRC), or failing to ensure licensed supervision of staff.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants Act (Canada) and the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations, s.91, unauthorized representation or advice for consideration is an offence; on summary conviction, a fine of up to CAD 100,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 2 years; on indictment, imprisonment up to 5 years. The College can seek cease-and-desist orders, injunctions and administrative monetary penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A corporate general partner cannot itself hold an RCIC licence; the licensed individual must be a principal of the licensed entity. Unlicensed partners who exercise control over immigration-consulting employees are personally exposed to prosecution, and the Ontario court may pierce the LP to hold each general partner and controlling limited partner liable for fines, restitution, and litigation costs.
